haiku-low.q1: A pull request runs build and unit tests only, and never deploys. Merging to main starts a run, which can deploy to staging and production.
haiku-low.q2: Both deploy the same image, built once, tagged with the commit SHA and pushed to registry.internal/shop-api. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry, and a second failure ends the run. Unit test failure ends the run immediately, with no retry.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs its previous_tag image, after deploy.sh rollback sets current_tag from it. The image is found by reading /deploy/staging/previous_tag in SSM.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members other than the commit author may approve. If no one decides within 72 hours, the run expires, is announced, and production stays untouched.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deop.sh writes them only after a successful stable rollout. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Canary-off runs and the run ends. Stable stays on its old image, SSM tags are unchanged, and applied forward-only migrations remain in the database.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is superseded: cancelled and announced in #deploys, if it is still waiting for approval or the window. A run that has started its canary is never superseded.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window, it waits for the next Monday to Thursday 09:00 UTC opening and can still be superseded. Behaviour when another production deploy holds the lock: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: Prometheus canary 5xx ratio, the share of canary requests failing over the last minute. Checked every 30 seconds for 15 minutes. Failure: any reading above 1 percent, or two empty readings in a row.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The document does not say how approvers are notified, or what information they receive to decide.
haiku-low.q12: Stable rollout failure runs kubectl rollout undo on that deployment, with SSM unchanged. It restores the pods that ran before, matching SSM. Rollback would move to an older tag and leave SSM wrong.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs the build (image not pushed) and unit tests (make test-unit); it never deploys. A merge to main starts a run, which can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image, built once at merge and tagged with the commit SHA (registry.internal/shop-api:SHA). Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: one automatic retry (known flaky test); if the retry fails, the run ends and is announced. Unit test failure: no retry, the run ends (announced).
sonnet.q4: The run runs `deploy.sh rollback staging`, which sets the staging image back to SSM staging previous_tag (the tag that ran before the current one). The run then ends, releases the staging lock and announces.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, never the author of the merged commit. If no decision within 72 hours, the run expires, is announced, production stays untouched on its current tag (staging keeps the new tag).
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout (stable only; canary is never recorded). Rollback changes current_tag from previous_tag but leaves previous_tag unchanged.
sonnet.q7: Stable is untouched and still on its old image; canary is turned off with deploy.sh canary-off; SSM tags are unchanged (canary is never recorded and tags are written only after the stable rollout). The database keeps the migrations already applied (production migrated before the canary), since migrations are forward-only with no undo; they must work with the previous image.
sonnet.q8: When the newer run is approved, every older run still waiting for approval or for the window is superseded: cancelled and announced in #deploys. A run that has already started its canary is never superseded.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits for the next Mon-Thu 09:00 UTC opening (and can still be superseded meanwhile). While another production deploy is in progress: NOT STATED beyond the production lock allowing only one production deploy at a time (the document does not say whether it queues or fails).
sonnet.q10: Measured: the canary's 5xx ratio (share of canary requests returning 5xx over the last minute). Prometheus is queried (expression from environments.md) every 30 seconds for 15 minutes (30 readings). Failure: any reading above 0.01 (1 percent), or 2 empty readings in a row (no traffic); then deploy.sh canary-off and the run ends.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document does not say how approvers are notified or what information they get.
sonnet.q12: Use `kubectl rollout undo` on the stable shop-api deployment (staging or production), restoring the pods that ran before the failed rollout. Reason: deploy.sh stops before writing SSM tags, so SSM still names the old tag as current; undo matches SSM, whereas `deploy.sh rollback` would move to previous_tag, which is older than what was running, and leave SSM wrong. In production, canary-off follows.
